title: Improving system safety with Temporal Logic of Actions (TLA+)
summary: Formal verification never seemed worth it: writing a faithful TLA+ spec took too long. But now agents can write the spec from your code. We tried it on the rebuilt Depot Registry garbage collector, and the model checker found something our tests and reviews didn't: a race that could delete live data.
body_markdown: Versioning isn't there to track changes to a blob, since the bytes never change in place. It's there to make deletion safe. Garbage collection has to remove unreferenced blobs, but references live in MySQL while the bytes live in S3, and no transaction spans both. That gap lets a client re-push a blob at the same moment GC decides to delete it. Versioning turns "delete this key" into "delete exactly the version I inspected," so GC removes the old version and leaves the newly pushed one untouched.
